description: A statute of limitation is a deadline for filing suit. In Georgia, a child injured in an auto accident is given until their 20th birthday to settle or sue.
shortAnswer: The statute of limitation is generally tolled on a minor's claim until the child turns 18. In Georgia, adults injured in an automobile accident are given 2 years to either settle their claim or file a lawsuit, yet a child injured in that same accident would be given until their 20th birthday to settle or sue.

faq.q: What does it mean when a statute of limitation is “tolled”?
faq.a: Tolling means that an injured person is given more time before the statute of limitation expires or “runs out.” The law speaks of tolling in terms of legal disability, and one such disability is being a minor.

faq.q: What is the deadline for a child sexual abuse or medical malpractice claim in Georgia?
faq.a: Children who are the victims of sexual abuse are given until their 23rd birthday to settle or sue. For malpractice occurring before the child's fifth birthday, the child's suit must be filed by the seventh birthday. For medical malpractice occurring after the fifth birthday, the limitation period is two years from the date of the malpractice.

faq.q: When must parents file a claim for their child's medical expenses in Georgia?
faq.a: Georgia law views any medical or necessary expenses arising from an injury to a child as belonging to the parents of that child, not the child itself. Suits for a parent's claim for a child's medical expenses should be filed within two years of the date of injury, even when no medical malpractice was involved.

faq.q: Is there a shorter deadline for a child injury claim against a city, county or state?
faq.a: Ante litem notices are required anytime you have a claim against a governmental entity, such as Cities, Counties, States, or the federal government. If you fail to notify the right department in the proper manner, you and your child's claim will be forever barred. Some of these deadlines are as short as six months from the date of injury.
